clue.text: Church with abnormal fear of the beetle

indicators.note: abnormal means out of its usual order, so the letters of the word fear are rearranged

explanation.surface: A churchgoer with an irrational dread of beetles.
explanation.definitionFit: The cockchafer and rose chafer are species of scarab beetle, so a chafer is a kind of beetle.

clue.text: Guide at the top hated one to slip

indicators.note: to slip means to slide out of place, so the letters of hated one are rearranged

explanation.surface: A guide on the summit disliked one person losing their footing.
explanation.definitionFit: A head-note is a note placed at the start of a chapter or page, guiding the reader at the top.

clue.text: Beef producers ready to market thick soup

parts.note: fat means thick, as in a fat book
stock is the liquid base for soup

explanation.surface: Cattle farmers are about to sell a hearty broth.
explanation.definitionFit: Fatstock are livestock fattened up for slaughter, ready to be sold as meat.

clue.text: Crumbling skull reportedly found in part of royal park

parts.note: something crumbling with decay is rotten
skull is pronounced like scull, and to scull a boat is to row it

explanation.surface: A decaying skull is discovered in a London park.
explanation.walkthrough: ROTTEN ROW is a riding track in Hyde Park, a royal park in London. The sound step works on skull, giving scull, which then means ROW.
explanation.definitionFit: Rotten Row is a broad track along the south side of Hyde Park, one of London's royal parks.

clue.text: Choppers caught deserters

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
deserters are people who leave, leavers

explanation.surface: Helicopter crews who have fled are arrested.
explanation.definitionFit: Butchers' heavy chopping knives are called cleavers, so choppers is a synonym.

clue.text: Mate on the run given a way to climb down?

parts.note: a mate is a companion
a run in tights or stockings is a ladder

explanation.surface: A partner in flight given an escape route.
explanation.walkthrough: A run in British usage is a ladder in stockings.
explanation.definitionFit: A companion ladder is the ship's stair from the deck down to the cabins, a means of descending.

clue.text: Prompt car signal

parts.note: auto is short for automobile, a car
a cue is a signal to act

explanation.definitionFit: An Autocue is a teleprompter, the screen that prompts presenters with their script.

clue.text: Fabric cut up and checked

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means the letters are read from the bottom, so the whole is reversed

parts.note: denim is a hard-wearing cotton fabric
to axe is to cut

explanation.surface: Cloth has been slashed and then inspected.
explanation.definitionFit: To have examined something is to have inspected it closely, the same as having checked it.

clue.text: Drug includes directions on recipient's case

indicators.note: in a down entry on means placed above, so the directions come before the grammatical case

parts.note: S and E are compass points, south and east
the dative is the grammatical case of the indirect object, the receiver

explanation.surface: A drug label gives instructions about the patient's condition.
explanation.walkthrough: The dative is the grammatical case of the receiver, as in 'give HIM the book'.
explanation.definitionFit: A sedative is a calming medicine, a kind of drug.

clue.text: Handyman happening to ring corporation

parts.note: a happening, something that actually occurred, is a fact
a ring is round, the shape of the letter O
corporation is an old jocular word for a pot belly, a tum

explanation.surface: A handyman event involves encircling a company.
explanation.walkthrough: 'corporation' here is the old humorous word for a large stomach, not a business.
explanation.definitionFit: A factotum is a person employed to do all kinds of jobs, a general handyman.

clue.text: Leave high and dry in lock

definitions.meaning: to leave someone stuck and helpless, as a ship run aground
a lock of hair, a single thread or tress

explanation.definitionFit: To strand is to leave helpless, and a strand is a single tress of hair, a lock.

clue.text: Hate a man channelled into great curse

indicators.note: channelled suggests being directed into a new form, so the letters of hate a man are rearranged

explanation.surface: Hatred for a man is directed into a terrible curse.
explanation.definitionFit: An anathema is a formal ecclesiastical ban or a solemn curse of excommunication.

clue.text: Second reviewer's opinion about page of writing

indicators.note: about means going around, so the letters for the critique surround the page letter

parts.note: a crit is a critique, a reviewer's verdict

explanation.surface: A second critic offers a view on a page of written work.
explanation.definitionFit: Script means handwriting or written text, the characters set down on paper.

clue.text: Stanhope's bearing

definitions.meaning: a stanhope is a light open horse-drawn vehicle; here the 's stands for is

explanation.walkthrough: A stanhope is a light, open, one-seat horse-drawn gig named after Fitzroy Stanhope.
explanation.definitionFit: A stanhope is a type of horse-drawn vehicle, and carriage also means the way a person holds the body.

clue.text: Government stock of gold trimmed

definitions.meaning: UK government bonds, considered very safe investments
having edges trimmed with gold leaf

explanation.definitionFit: Gilt-edged securities are British government bonds, and gilt-edged pages are trimmed with gold.

clue.text: Made skiffle section stand for music

indicators.note: a section is a part cut out of something, so the letters are taken from inside the words Made skiffle

explanation.surface: Someone created a skiffle part to be performed.
explanation.definitionFit: In an orchestra a music desk is the stand holding the players' sheet music.

clue.text: This wine-bottle should give one no grounds for complaint

definitions.text: This wine-bottle should give one no grounds for complaint

parts.words: This wine-bottle should give one no grounds for complaint
parts.note: grounds is read as sediment: pouring wine into this vessel leaves the dregs behind

explanation.definitionFit: A glass vessel into which wine is poured off its sediment, leaving no dregs.

clue.text: Gentle cleansing agent — use flannel

definitions.meaning: flannel is British slang for flattering, smooth talk

explanation.definitionFit: Soft soap is a mild cleanser, and to soft-soap someone is to flatter them; flannel is British slang for evasive smooth talk.

clue.text: Matinee favourite said to be resting

indicators.note: said means spoken, so we want a word that is pronounced like the word for a star of the stage

parts.note: a matinee idol is a handsome actor adored by audiences

explanation.surface: A star of afternoon shows is reported to be taking a break.
explanation.walkthrough: IDOL and IDLE sound the same.
explanation.definitionFit: An actor who is resting is out of work, that is unoccupied or inactive.

clue.text: Perfectionist's multiple contribution to suggestions box?

definitions.text: Perfectionist's multiple contribution to suggestions box?

parts.words: Perfectionist's multiple contribution to suggestions box?
parts.note: a perfectionist is defined, and the word split in two is also a list of ideas dropped in a suggestions box

explanation.definitionFit: Someone striving after perfection, whose name split up describes a catalogue of proposals.

clue.text: Meal taking an age if it's not cut short

definitions.text: Meal taking an age if it's not cut short

parts.words: Meal taking an age if it's not cut short
parts.note: a midday meal plus a word for an age gives the full, uncut form of the shortened meal name

explanation.definitionFit: A formal midday meal, whose everyday name is its shortened form.

clue.text: Dinghy at first was ahead, catching breeze, but petered out

indicators.note: catching means holding something inside, so the letters for breeze sit within the outer pieces
at first means just the opening letter of Dinghy is used

parts.note: to have been in front is to have led
a breeze is a wind

explanation.surface: A sailing race where a dinghy in the lead caught a gust but then faded.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dinghy at first' sets a sailing scene, but it only supplies its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Dwindled means diminished gradually, just as something that petered out faded away.

clue.text: Comparatively holy prophet

definitions.meaning: more godly, the comparative of an adjective for heavenly
a seer who foretells the future

explanation.definitionFit: Diviner is the comparative of divine, more holy, and a diviner is a soothsayer.

clue.text: Lively voice

definitions.meaning: in grammar, the voice where the subject performs the action, as opposed to passive

explanation.definitionFit: Active means energetic, and the active voice is the grammatical form where the subject acts.

clue.text: Suspension of a governor who's deployed cane

parts.note: a bey was a governor of a province in the Ottoman Empire

indicators.note: deployed means spread out and arranged in a new way, so the letters of cane are rearranged

explanation.surface: A ruler is suspended from office for having used a cane.
explanation.definitionFit: Abeyance is a state of temporary suspension or disuse, as with a law held in abeyance.

clue.text: Prickly as an old character?

definitions.meaning: the thorn is an Old English runic letter, so a word meaning like that letter

explanation.walkthrough: Thorn was a letter used in Old English for the th sound.
explanation.definitionFit: Thorny means spiny, and whimsically it means resembling thorn, the obsolete letter of Old English.

clue.text: Exhausted hound tried detour

parts.note: a hound is a dog

indicators.note: a detour is a roundabout route, suggesting the letters of tried go a different way round

explanation.surface: A tired dog took a longer way home.
explanation.definitionFit: Dog-tired is an idiom for utterly worn out, as exhausted as possible.

clue.text: Person who interviews one very big noise after another

definitions.meaning: a journalist who questions people for a story

definitions.text: one very big noise after another
definitions.meaning: a report is a loud bang, so something making reports one after another, like a gun

explanation.definitionFit: A journalist questions sources for news, and a report is also a loud explosion, so this suggests a thing producing bangs.

clue.text: Taking out becoming old hat

definitions.meaning: taking someone out on romantic outings
growing out of fashion, beginning to look old

explanation.definitionFit: Dating means courting someone, and a style that is dating is going out of fashion.
